To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of self-organized map (SOM) clustering of NCI 60 cell line screening data revealed a cluster of compounds which included known complex I inhibitors, (2) 5 of 10 compounds in this cluster were complex I inhibitors with IC50's of 1.3-5.4 nM in bovine heart SMP, (3) 4 of these 5 compounds were cytotoxic to leukemia cells in the NCI 60 panel, and

data mining of the NCI's SOM anticancer screen data reveals that mitochondrial complex I inhibitors are cytotoxic to leukemia cells and that the five most potent complex I inhibitors identified by this strategy are also the most cytotoxic to leukemia K562 cells.
data mining of the NCI's anticarcinogenic screening data revealed mitochondrial complex I inhibitors with antiproliferative activity toward leukemia cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of mitochondrial complex I inhibitors with anticancer activity and the use of SOMs to identify compounds which may be complex I inhibitors.
identifying novel compounds with anticancer activity.
the development and application of data mining techniques in the discovery and design of novel chemotherapeutic agents for the treatment of cancer.

we have demonstrated the utility of SOM data for the identification of novel mitochondrial complex I inhibitors which may have anticancer activity.
we have identified five new complex I inhibitors with IC50 values of 0.2-0.5 nM in bovine heart SMP and that they were cytostatic toward K562 cells with IC50's ranging between 0.2 and 2.0 microM.

data mining of the NCI's anticancercell line screen data can be a valuable tool for the identification of new anticancer agents.
